name: Extrapelvic Endometriosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnosis of Extrapelvic Endometriosis

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of endometrial glands and stroma outside the pelvic cavity
Imaging evidence (MRI, ultrasound, CT) of lesions in extrapelvic locations
Cyclic or chronic symptoms correlating with menstrual cycle in extrapelvic sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus either imaging evidence or characteristic clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathology; imaging and clinical features support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cyclic chest pain associated with menstruation

pathognomonic.notes: Recurrent pneumothorax linked to menstrual cycle
Blood in urine during menstruation due to urinary tract involvement

common.symptomName: Cyclic abdominal wall mass with tenderness
searchTerms: tender abdominal wall lump during cycle

common.notes: Painful defecation linked to bowel endometriosis
Pain during intercourse related to extrapelvic lesions

occasional.symptomName: Neuropathic pain in affected peripheral nerves
occasional.notes: Due to nerve infiltration by endometrial tissue
Sciatic nerve involvement causing radiating leg pain

occasional.symptomName: Cyclic hemoptysis with pleuritic chest pain
searchTerms: chest pain with bloody sputum during cycle

occasional.notes: Urinary symptoms linked to bladder endometriosis

laboratory: Elevated CA-125 levels in some cases
Cytology showing endometrial cells in pleural or peritoneal fluid
imaging: CT scan identifying thoracic or abdominal lesions
Ultrasound detecting abdominal wall or bladder masses
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; familial clustering reported
other: Histopathological confirmation with endometrial glands and stroma outside pelvic cavity
Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) findings in thoracic cases

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of cyclic pattern linked to menstruation
No histological evidence of endometrial tissue
Presence of infection markers in urine
Histology showing fibrous tissue without endometrial glands

redFlags: Recurrent catamenial pneumothorax with respiratory distress
Progressive neurological deficits with cyclical pattern
Severe hematuria or hemoptysis coinciding with menstruation
references: Vercellini P, et al. Extrapelvic endometriosis: clinical features and pathogenesis. Fertil Steril. 2014.
Nezhat C, et al. Thoracic endometriosis syndrome: a review of diagnosis and management. J Minim Invasive Gynecol. 2017.
